comment: SurfaceRelay 0.1 runtime binding conformance scenarios (T-003). kind=schema scenarios are executable today: scripts/validate.py asserts their fixture passes or fails via the fixture manifest. kind=runtime scenarios are semantic (schema-valid but not executable / not permitted); they are documented here and become executable conformance in T-604/T-701 when real runtimes exist. schema-invalid is NOT the same as runtime-stale.

scenarios.detail: A page-scoped binding is structurally valid.
A component-scoped binding is structurally valid.
A session-scoped binding is structurally valid; session authority is a runtime reference, never caller input.
A persistent binding is structurally valid; persistent never means permanent (D-023).
Unknown lifecycle value is rejected by schema.
A binding without an exact action version is rejected by schema; bindings never float across versions (D-022).
A schema-valid binding whose expiresAt has passed must be rejected at invocation time. Cumulative validity (D-024): expiry wins independently of lifecycle state.

A schema-valid, well-formed driver string that is not explicitly registered must fail closed with no fallback (D-016). JSON Schema cannot express registry membership by design; the registry check is runtime semantics.
A schema-valid binding whose referenced action id+version is not registered (or no longer matches) must fail closed even though the document is structurally valid.
A component-scoped binding whose component instance was unmounted/destroyed/replaced must fail closed; a rerender of the same instance may remain valid. The issuing adapter detects lifecycle end.

Old binding + replacement component (same class, method name, DOM position, or business record) must NOT execute; the old binding returns stale, and the replacement requires a newly issued binding ID (D-022/D-025).
An unknown bindingId must fail closed. A binding ID is a reference, never proof of authorization by itself (D-022).
